Definition: from G4862 and G118; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly:--labour with, strive together for.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Philippians to stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel, and he names the women who laboured with him in the gospel. Striving together is not competition but a team pulling one rope, and the gospel is the cause worth the strain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the faith is worth striving for together, and I hold that a church pulling one rope will not be pulled apart.
